content.comment_body: According to the specifications, the [product_name] RTD module only supports PT100 sensors within a temperature range of -50°C to 200°C. I need to measure a boiler's internal temperature up to 450°C, which requires a higher-range PT100 sensor. Online, there are many PT100 sensors available that cover temperatures from -20°C to 400/450°C. How can I connect a PT100 sensor rated up to 450°C to the [product_name] RTD module with a 200°C limit? Or is there an alternative way to use these higher-temperature PT100 sensors?

Are you certain the sensor is actually a PT type? Try measuring both the temperature and the resistance at the sensor. Comparing the resistance value at the measured temperature against a PT100 table will confirm whether the sensor is truly a PT100.

Hello, I currently have three RTD modules connected to standard PT100 sensors and everything works fine within the 200°C range. I haven't purchased a 450°C sensor yet, but I'm searching for one similar to those found on auction sites: [url]. Do you think these are real PT100 sensors? They also offer a version labeled 'K' with a range of -50°C to 450°C. Can this PT100 sensor be connected?

A PT100 sensor functions as a resistor that changes value based on temperature. The PT sensor you are considering should operate in the -50°C to 400°C range. When connected to the [product_name] RTD module, only resistance values corresponding to -50°C to 200°C are interpreted; temperatures above 200°C will be displayed as 200°C by the module. To cover the range from -50°C to 400°C, you'll need an external temperature transmitter that outputs a signal such as 0 to 10V or 0/4 to 20mA. Note that a sensor labeled 'K' refers to a thermocouple, not a PT sensor, and can't be used directly. For thermocouples, you would require an external transmitter and appropriate compensation wiring.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users determined that while the [product_name] RTD module is compatible with PT100 sensors, its temperature measurement stops at 200°C. This limitation prevents accurate readings of higher temperatures, such as those required for boiler fire monitoring up to 450°C. Although higher-range PT100 sensors exist, the module’s hardware restricts effective use beyond its stated limits, potentially causing readings to cap or become unreliable above 200°C.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is looking for a solution that allows the [product_name] RTD module to read temperatures up to 450°C from a high-range PT100 sensor, or guidance on alternative methods for obtaining these measurements.
